genZNote: The name means 'that which bends up' in the Kimakonde language — a direct reference to the joint pain that can linger for months.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Maintained in a mosquito-human (urban) or mosquito-primate (sylvatic) transmission cycle
habitat.hostAssociation: Transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, the same vectors as dengue and Zika
habitat.reservoir: Humans (urban cycle) and non-human primates (sylvatic cycle in parts of Africa)

identificationClues: Diagnosed by RT-PCR early in illness or serology (IgM) after the first week
High fever with severe, often debilitating polyarthralgia/arthritis — frequently more prominent and prolonged than in dengue
Transmitted by the same Aedes mosquitoes responsible for dengue and Zika, so co-circulation and overlapping symptoms are common in endemic areas
Joint pain can persist for weeks to months after the acute illness resolves, a distinguishing clinical feature

diseases: Chikungunya fever — sudden high fever, severe polyarthralgia/arthritis (often symmetric, affecting hands/wrists/ankles), rash, and headache; joint symptoms can become chronic and debilitating
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus mosquito
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic and epidemic in parts of Africa, Asia, and increasingly the Americas following its introduction to the Caribbean; outbreaks often overlap geographically and temporally with dengue and Zika due to shared mosquito vectors
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Distinguishing chikungunya from dengue and Zika based on symptoms alone is difficult since all three share vectors and overlapping presentations; specific RT-PCR or serologic testing is needed for confirmation

examFacts.importantDisease: Chikungunya fever — severe, often prolonged polyarthralgia
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: An Aedes-transmitted alphavirus causing unusually severe and often prolonged joint pain, more prominent than the arthralgia seen with dengue or Zika
